newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FUEL SHORTAGE HITS ROMANIA AGRICULTURE.
newsitem.headline: FUEL SHORTAGE HITS ROMANIA AGRICULTURE.

text.p: A fuel shortage has hit Romania's farming sector, risking delays in seasonal farm work, an agriculture ministry official said on Thursday.

The farming sector received only 27 percent of the planned 24,000 tonnes over September 1-7, said the official, who asked not to be named, in a repeat of problems that have plagued agriculture throughout the summer.
"The situation is quite bad and i think that many farming works will be delayed," said the official.
The farming sector needed some 90,000 tonnes of fuel this month to ensure ploughing and late harvests can continue, he added.

An acute hard currency shortage has forced Romania to cut its crude oil imports over the past months. Refineries are working below capacity and distribution of fuel supplies has been disrupted across the country.
Last week, scores of cars using unleaded petrol queued for days outside filling stations in Bucharest.

The official said many state-run farms lacked funds to buy the necessary fuel while the state farming sector owed Peco SA fuel retailer some 12.8 billion for fuel supplied in the past weeks. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
